statement: A general smooth complex plane curve of degree d≥4 has d(d−2)(d²−9)/2 ordinary bitangent lines.

source.location: Section7, printed p.197; opening historical discussion p.193
source.version: Original Philosophical Transactions149(1859),193–212; JSTOR original-journal scan

notes:
The paper credits Plücker 1834 for the count. Cayley supplies an analytic derivation, not priority for the numerical formula. Generic smoothness and ordinary contact are essential.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_3c44d1090943e802; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

Originality audit: Plücker (1834) is associated with the announced count, and Cayley (1859) with this record’s analytic derivation. These are distinct contributions.

Cayley’s opening paragraph explicitly attributes the numerical double-tangent formula to Plücker 1834. Cayley remains cited for the analytical contact-curve construction included in this record.

Section7 obtains a contact-point curve of degree(d−2)(d²−9), then divides its intersection count with the degree-d curve by two to give d(d−2)(d²−9)/2 bitangents.

The following bibliography supplies historical attribution or supporting background for the result. Julius Plücker, Solution d'une question fondamentale concernant la théorie générale des courbes. (1834, plucker_1834_curve_formula).
scope: General smooth complex projective plane curves of degree d≥4, ordinary bitangents with two distinct contact points.
